title: Geometric Constructions
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Geometric Constructions. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Triangle construction by SSS, SAS and ASA

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Permitted construction tools

Classical constructions use an unmarked straightedge to draw a line through known points and a compass to copy a radius. Keep the compass width fixed when transferring equal distances; label construction arcs and intersections clearly.

Bisectors and standard angles

A perpendicular bisector passes through a segment's midpoint at 90 degrees. Points on it are equidistant from the segment endpoints. An angle bisector divides an angle into two equal angles; its points are equidistant from the two arms.

Triangle construction

Three side lengths construct a unique triangle when they satisfy the triangle inequality. Two sides and their included angle (SAS), or two angles and a corresponding side (\(ASA/AAS\)), also determine a triangle. An SSA specification can be ambiguous.

Worked construction: To construct the perpendicular bisector of segment (AB), draw equal-radius arcs centered at A and B using a radius greater than half (AB). Join the two arc intersection points; this line bisects (AB) at right angles.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Use the same compass opening for paired arcs that must be equal.
  • Choose a radius large enough for the arcs to intersect on both sides.
  • Do not erase the arcs: they show why the construction is valid.
  • Check triangle data with the triangle inequality before drawing.
  • Distinguish an angle bisector from a perpendicular bisector.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• A point on a perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the two endpoints.
  • A point on an angle bisector is equidistant from the angle's sides.
  • Constructible angles include 60, 90, 30 and 45 degrees using standard steps.
  • Three lengths form a triangle only when the sum of any two exceeds the third.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    A point lies on the perpendicular bisector of segment (AB). Which statement must be true?

    1. It is closer to (\(A\))
    2. It is closer to (\(B\))
    3. Its distances to (\(A\)) and (\(B\)) are equal
    4. It lies at the midpoint
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: Its distances to (\(A\)) and (\(B\)) are equal

    Every point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the segment's endpoints. The point need not be the midpoint.

  2. Core:

    To construct the perpendicular bisector of (AB) using equal arcs from both endpoints, what must be true about the arc radius?

    1. Less than half of (AB)
    2. Exactly half of (AB)
    3. Greater than half of (AB)
    4. It must equal (AB)
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: Greater than half of (AB)

    A radius greater than half the segment makes the arcs intersect above and below (AB); joining those intersections gives the perpendicular bisector.

  3. Foundation:

    What is the locus of points equidistant from the endpoints of a fixed segment?

    1. A circle centered at an endpoint
    2. The perpendicular bisector
    3. A parallel line
    4. The segment itself
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: The perpendicular bisector

    Every point equidistant from both endpoints lies on the segment's perpendicular bisector.

  4. Standard:

    Which set of side lengths cannot form a triangle?

    1. (\(4,5,6\))
    2. (\(3,4,6\))
    3. (\(5,5,9\))
    4. (\(2,3,6\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(2,3,6\))

    The sum of the two shorter sides must exceed the longest side. Here (\(2+3=5<6\)), so no triangle is possible.

  5. Challenge:

    Two sides and their included angle are given. Which criterion determines the triangle uniquely?

    1. (SSS)
    2. (SAS)
    3. (SSA in every case)
    4. One side only
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (SAS)

    Two sides and the included angle determine a unique triangle by the SAS congruence criterion.
